name: Kuk Early Agricultural Site
description: In the cool highlands of Papua New Guinea, about 12 km northeast of Mount Hagen, Kuk is a swampy valley where people were digging drainage ditches with wooden tools thousands of years ago. Buried ditches and planting mounds show farming here for at least 7,000 years, possibly far longer. It is one of the few places where agriculture arose independently, with taro among the early crops.
